scholarships.title: NTHU International Student Scholarship
scholarships.official_source: National Tsing Hua University (NTHU), Office of Global Affairs

existing.description: The NTHU International Student Scholarship, funded by the Office of Global Affairs at National Tsing Hua University, is applied for through the same online system as admission to an NTHU international degree programme. It provides a full tuition and credit-fee waiver plus a tiered monthly stipend: NTD 20,000 to 40,000 per month for doctoral students, NTD 10,000 per month for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences or the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with supervisors from that college, and NTD 5,000 per month for master and bachelor students. It is restricted to applicants who and whose parents have always held foreign nationality and never held Taiwan nationality, excludes overseas Chinese student status, and is not available for Medicine, Dentistry, Traditional Chinese Medicine, the College of Semiconductor or ICDF programmes.
eligibility: Applicants and their parents must all hold foreign nationality and have never held Republic of China (Taiwan) nationality.
Must not have studied in Taiwan under overseas Chinese student status.
Those who previously studied in Taiwan under the Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan may reapply, but only once, and only for NTHU undergraduate programmes.
Applicants may not apply for programmes in Medicine, Dentistry or Traditional Chinese Medicine; this limitation does not apply to graduate programmes.
Foreign students currently studying in Taiwan who meet these criteria may apply through the same process as overseas international applicants.
The scholarship is not available for the College of Semiconductor and for ICDF programmes.
Admission to the chosen NTHU degree programme is required, since the scholarship is applied for through the admission system.
existing.eligibility_summary: International applicants, admitted by NTHU under the MOE Regulations Regarding International Students Undertaking Studies in Taiwan. Applicants and their parents must all hold foreign nationality and have never held Taiwan nationality, and must not have previously studied in Taiwan as an overseas Chinese student. The scholarship is not available for the College of Semiconductor and ICDF programmes.
benefits: Doctoral students: NTD 20,000 to 40,000 per month.
Doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, or in the International Intercollegiate PhD Program with supervisors from that college: NTD 10,000 per month.
coverage: Full tuition and credit fee waiver.
Monthly stipend of NTD 5,000 for bachelor students.
Monthly stipend of NTD 5,000 for master students.
Monthly stipend of NTD 20,000 to 40,000 for doctoral students.
Monthly stipend of NTD 10,000 for doctoral students in the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, or in the International Intercollegiate PhD Program whose supervisors are from that college.
requirements: Apply through the NTHU International Student Online Application System for an international degree programme.
Select 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship' in the application.
Meet NTHU's international applicant nationality and residency conditions.
Not apply for Medicine, Dentistry or Traditional Chinese Medicine programmes at undergraduate level, nor for the College of Semiconductor or ICDF programmes.
Upload and submit all required documents before the intake's application deadline.
documents: All documents required for admission to the international degree programme, uploaded through the NTHU International Student Online Application System
Proof of awarded scholarship, where the applicant already holds one
application_method: Apply through the NTHU International Student Online Application System used for international degree programme applications.
Tick the portal option 'Apply for NTHU international student scholarship' when submitting the application.
Scholarship results are announced separately from admission results, in late December for the published Spring 2027 intake.
existing.selection_notes: The scholarship is applied for through the admission system, so admission and scholarship decisions are linked. Applicants admitted to an ICDF-funded programme only cannot receive this scholarship; applicants admitted to both an ICDF and a non-ICDF programme may receive it for the non-ICDF programme only, subject to the admitted list.
existing.best_fit: International applicants admitted to an NTHU degree programme outside Medicine, Dentistry, Traditional Chinese Medicine, the College of Semiconductor and ICDF programmes, with doctoral candidates attracting by far the largest award.
existing.notes: The stipend is strongly tiered by degree level: doctoral students receive NTD 20,000 to 40,000 per month, master and bachelor students only NTD 5,000 per month. The tuition and credit-fee waiver is the common component across all levels. Scholarship results are published separately from admission results. Applicants to ICDF-funded programmes should note the interaction rules: an ICDF scholarship holder cannot also receive this award, and someone admitted to both an ICDF and a non-ICDF programme may receive it only for the non-ICDF programme. NTHU publishes a financial-certificate requirement of more than USD 4,000 equivalent for applicants who are not ICDF scholarship holders.
existing.duration: Follows the duration of the degree programme enrolled in; no separate award period is published.
existing.application_period: Applied for together with the international degree programme admission, in NTHU's published intake windows. The published Spring 2027 international degree application period was 3 August to 30 September 2026 (15:00 Taiwan time), with admission results on 1 December 2026 and scholarship results in late December 2026.
existing.deadline_display: The scholarship has no separate deadline: NTHU instructs applicants to 'Apply scholarship through the same online system for international degree programs', so the deadline is the admission deadline for the relevant intake. NTHU's published Spring 2027 international degree application period was 3 August to 30 September 2026 at 15:00 Taiwan time, which has closed.
existing.program_type: University scholarship for international degree students combining a full tuition and credit-fee waiver with a tiered monthly stipend

scholarships.title: NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students
scholarships.official_source: National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University (NYCU), Office of International Affairs, Division of International Talent Cultivation

existing.description: The NYCU Elite Ph.D. Scholarship for New Students awards a monthly stipend of NT$33,000 together with a tuition waiver for two years to new doctoral students at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University who have outstanding grades and hold no other scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. It is not open to direct application: NYCU states that the award is made on the basis of recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee. Recipients must submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible, and the stipend is in principle deposited on the 10th of each month. The tuition waiver covers basic tuition only, with dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees remaining payable.
eligibility: Must be a new Ph.D. student at National Yang Ming Chiao Tung University.
Must not have received any scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government.
Must be nominated by the candidate's college and selected by the scholarship committee; students cannot apply directly.
existing.eligibility_summary: New PhD students at NYCU with outstanding grades who have not received any scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government. Because the award is nomination-based, eligibility is assessed through the college rather than by direct application.
benefits: Full tuition waiver for two years.
In principle, the monthly stipend is deposited on the 10th of each month.
coverage: Not covered: dormitory, insurance and campus facility incidental fees, which remain payable by the student.
requirements: Be a new Ph.D. student at NYCU with outstanding grades.
Not hold any scholarship or grant from the Taiwan government.
Be nominated by the college and selected by the scholarship committee.
As a recipient, submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts every semester before the specified deadline.
Renew during the application period announced by the OIA.
documents: Semester transcripts (submitted each semester to remain eligible)
Tuition payment receipts (submitted each semester to remain eligible)
application_method: There is no student application. The candidate is nominated by their college and the award is decided by the NYCU scholarship committee.
Existing recipients submit semester transcripts and tuition payment receipts before the specified per-semester deadline to be eligible in the following semester.
Renewal is processed during the application period announced by the OIA, during which applicants must complete the scholarship renewal requirements.
existing.selection_notes: The award is based on recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee, not on a student application. Full terms are set out in NYCU's scholarship regulations.
existing.best_fit: New doctoral candidates admitted to NYCU with outstanding academic records who hold no other Taiwan government scholarship or grant, and whose college is willing to nominate them.
existing.notes: This is a nomination-based award, so applicants cannot apply for it and cannot select it on an application form. It is distinct from the general NYCU International Student Scholarship, which students apply for through the OIA application system in published windows (the Spring 2027 New Students Scholarship window published on the system was 10 August 2026 to 13 November 2026) and whose stipend amounts are flexibly adjusted. The tuition waiver covers basic tuition only: NYCU's own system states that dormitory, insurance and campus facility fees must still be paid, so this award should not be presented as fully funded. Holders of Taiwan Scholarships, ESP, UST, TIGP, NSNT, ICDF or NYCU Elite Ph.D. scholarships are all treated as government-funded and are mutually exclusive for the general NYCU scholarship.
existing.duration: Two years of monthly stipend plus tuition waiver, per NYCU's published 'Scholarship Content and Duration'.
existing.application_period: Not student-applied. New Ph.D. places are nominated by the candidate's college and reviewed by the scholarship committee within NYCU's doctoral admission cycle. Existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts each semester before a per-semester deadline to remain eligible in the following semester, and renewals are handled in the application period announced by the OIA.
existing.deadline_display: No application deadline exists for this award. NYCU states that the Elite Ph.D. Scholarship "is awarded based on recommendations from the college and a review by the scholarship committee, not through the application submitted by the students". The only recurring dates are the per-semester deadline by which existing recipients must submit transcripts and tuition payment receipts to stay eligible the following semester.
existing.program_type: University nomination-based doctoral scholarship (college recommendation and scholarship committee review, not a direct student application)
